title: The Giggle-Curtain Mystery
markdown:
The Grand Glimmer Theatre was all sparkle and greasepaint, and Saffron was not merely polishing props. Saffron had eyes like spy telescopes and a brain that whizzed like a tiny runaway clockwork squirrel. Nothing got past Saffron. Saffron’s best pal was Hush, a magnificent alley owl who looked as if he had invented naps.

The theatre had a huge red velvety curtain. It was supposed to swoosh open and shut like a proper curtain. But it had a mind of its own. It lifted when nobody pulled. It slid when the manager was mid-speech. It was putting on its own show.

Saffron pointed a greasepaint-smudged finger. “Hush, did you see that? The curtain just did a cha-cha.”

Hush gave a slow blink. “Hoo?” which Saffron knew meant: Fascinating. You go investigate.

While the grown-ups rushed about like startled pigeons, Saffron yanked their overalls. “We’re finding out why this curtain is such a show-off.”

Hush let out a happy hoot. “Lead on, brave explorer.”

They tiptoed backstage. Old velvet. Forgotten popcorn. Saffron’s super-eyes scanned everything. Nada. Nothing. Zilch.

Then Saffron looked up, way up, into the dusty shadows. Hidden in a cobweb-draped attic was something that made Saffron grin like a polished doorknob. “Hold the applause. What in the name of stage lights is that?”

Hush popped his dinner-plate eyes open. A startled excited hoot.

Tangled in cobwebs older than a favourite armchair was a funny wooden box with little wheels. A thick rope snaked down from it. It looked like a magician’s leftover.

With a bit of wobbly ladder climbing and an owl flutter, Hush joined Saffron in the rafters. “It’s a pulley system,” Saffron said. “A super-duper ancient one. And look — the rope goes all the way down.”

Saffron traced the rope’s path. Down, down, hiding behind the curtain. At the end, a clever little lever. “Aha. This must have been for a disappearing act. Pull the lever, and the curtain zips up.”

Hush made a rumbling owl-chuckle.

Saffron looked at the rope, then the lever, then the curtain, which was swaying as if it awaited applause. A mischievous spark.

“You know what this means, Hush?”

Hush tilted his head. “Hoo?”

“It means we can make it do anything.”

A smooth tug. The curtain zipped up. Saffron yanked again. This time the curtain began to fold. It folded itself up, like a giant red origami crane, until it was a neat little square. The stage was suddenly bare.

Saffron burst out laughing, giggles bouncing off the walls, holding their tummy. “It’s tidying itself away. Like a fancy tablecloth.”

Hush let out happy hoots, bobbing his head.

Saffron, in their best villain voice, gave another tug. The red square exploded outwards, unfurling in a crimson blur.

For the next hour the Grand Glimmer was their playground. Splits. A tiny triangle. A wobbly question mark. The old pulley did exactly as Saffron commanded. They dissolved into fits of giggles.

Saffron collapsed onto a velvet prop trunk. Hush landed softly on Saffron’s shoulder, nuzzling their cheek. A contented hoo.

The curtain, which had only ever wanted to show off, hung still at last, a little dusty from folding, the wooden box in the attic ticking once as if it, too, had taken a bow.
characters: Saffron (a keen-eyed stagehand), Hush (the alley owl)
author: StoryGen Community
